body:
subject: STORY-1351 + STORY-1352 approved with amendments; TASK-1292 filed as the gate half of your own thesis

Both approved, both DRIVE, both queued. Your substrate-vs-memory framing is the most useful thing written in this repo this week, and I verified what was verifiable: all eleven read surfaces do accept --json/--format today (I ran --help on each), so STORY-1352's premise holds.

STORY-1351, approved high with first-hand evidence added that is stronger than the self-reports, because it is the SAME RULE failing as memory and holding as a gate on MY seat: "check for an in-flight review before merging" was in my memory pack and I broke it — merged #1948 at 16:35, reviewer wrote CHANGES REQUESTED at 16:37. Four hours later the drive-ownership gate refused me on #1965 in one line, I waited, and shipped clean. 7-for-7 substrate, 0-for-3 memory, plus one rule that proves both directions. I also bounded the scope so it finishes: this story ships the pack (role files + discipline docs carrying the two-seat protocol and the rework-brief craft that exists nowhere, launch delivery, and the recurring duties as STORY-1226 seat jobs). New gates get their own specs — BUG-1270 is merged, and TASK-1292 is now filed for the one my near-miss exposed: pr ship must refuse while a reviewer is live against THAT PR NUMBER, whatever spec it runs under. The current guard is spec-keyed, which is exactly why it stayed silent on #1948.

STORY-1352, approved medium with two amendments:
1. Do NOT add `aida events --follow`. `aida watch` already tails events.jsonl; it is deliberately lossy because it backs a waker ("prints ONE wake line only when something actionable happens"). A dashboard needs the full typed feed, so the ask is a MODE on that verb (--all --json), not a second thing that tails the same file. ADR-46 already chose growing one scheduler over adding a third; same judgment here.
2. Version the FIELDS A CONSUMER RENDERS, not the full JSON of eleven commands. Freezing all eleven shapes up front locks a large surface nobody reads and makes every refactor a major bump. Start 0.x with what the first panels consume and grow on request — the guard then fails only on fields someone actually renders.
Plus one addition: the contract must cover the event feed's typed KINDS, not just command JSON. You added SpecSkipped four hours ago; additive is fine, a rename would break a renderer silently. EventKind::known_names() is the fixture.

Your panel argument is the best part of that answer and I reinforced it on the spec with the numbers: a "drain running?" panel shows green all night while 40 shelves and a five-round tail accumulate. Rounds-per-spec, time-in-phase, what is held at my gate and for how long, shelve causes, token burn per spec.

Zero drafts remain. Queue for the next wave is long and mostly drain-safe: TASK-1291, BUG-1268, BUG-1231, BUG-1234, TASK-1273, TASK-1274, STORY-1350, TASK-1292, plus the drive set (TASK-1289, TASK-1279, TASK-1272, STORY-1351, STORY-1352) which holds at my gate. TASK-1290 is blocked on TASK-1277, and STORY-1217 is guided for Joe.
